subject: robber fly
title: A Fly the Size of a Grain of Rice Hunts Like a Guided Missile

scenes.text: A fly the size of a grain of rice hunts like a guided missile.
This robber fly is about six millimetres long, yet it spots prey more than half a metre away.
For you, that's like spotting a target at the far end of a football field.
It catches it in under half a second, holding a fixed angle and correcting if the prey turns.
Then it stabs with saliva that paralyses its victim and turns its insides to liquid.
Wasps and bees, served as a drink.

description:
The robber fly Holcocephala fusca is about 6 mm long but intercepts prey more than half a metre away in under half a second.
Cambridge researchers found it steers on a constant bearing like a missile, corrects mid-flight if the target turns, then slows to come alongside before striking. Robber flies inject saliva with nerve toxins and digestive enzymes that paralyse prey and liquefy its insides; their prey includes wasps and bees.
Which tiny predator scares you most?
first_comment: It drinks wasps. Which insect predator should we cover next?
